title: Coordinate crypto-shredding and key-based redaction for analytics retention with deletion attestations
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: our analytics pipelines currently rely on logical deletion + tombstones and downstream scrubbing jobs. That model leaves two hard problems: (1) historical backups or derived aggregates can still contain PII even after logical deletion and (2) proving irrecoverable deletion to auditors is brittle. This ticket defines a coordinated crypto-shredding coordinator for analytics: wrap sensitive fields at ingest with per-tenant ephemeral data keys (DEKs) that are themselves wrapped by KMS-managed key-encryption-keys (KEKs). To delete data, we revoke/delete the KEK or the DEK material according to policy. Deleting the wrapping key makes wrapped ciphertext unrecoverable (crypto-shredding), providing stronger deletion guarantees and a compact deletion attestation for compliance.
acceptance_criteria: Ingest path supports configurable field-level wrapping: specify fields to DEK-wrap at pipeline source (Console telemetry, ingestion lambda, kafka producer).
Key lifecycle APIs implemented: create/deactivate/destroy DEKs and create/rotate KEKs using KMS/HSM integration and recorded in audit log.
Coordinator service that orchestrates delete-by-policy: can target tenant/route/time-range and revoke associated KEKs/DEKs and emit signed deletion attestations (hash anchored in audit log).
Backfill job that rewraps historical PII for existing partitions without causing downtime and bounded throughput impact (throttles + checkpointing).

Query/runtime compatibility: dashboards and aggregations function with wrapped fields via deterministic tokenization or server-side unwrap for authorized queries; unauthorized consumers cannot unwrap.
Compliance artifact generated: per-request deletion certificate containing scope, keys destroyed (by id), timestamp, audit-log anchors, and operator id.
Automated tests covering key destruction edge-cases, replica lag, and restore attempts after key deletion (should fail irrecoverably).
Performance budget: end-to-end ingest added latency <= 15ms p50 for wrapped fields under normal load; backfill CPU/IO cost within budget for a 30-day historical window.
proposal: Phase 1: Implement DEK wrapping on ingestion for Console telemetry and the main analytics producer. Store only ciphertext + metadata (wrapper key id, algorithm, nonce). Use AWS KMS (and HSM plugin for Private customers) to wrap/unwrap DEKs. Build a lightweight Coordinator microservice responsible for mapping tenancy->KEK->DEK sets, issuing delete workflows that transition keys from active->revoked->destroyed, and writing a signed attestation into the immutable audit log with a SHA256 anchor. Phase 2: Backfill rewrap job and dashboard integrations (deterministic tokens for joins). Phase 3: Legal-hold/escrow: support limited, auditable, escrow recovery via split-KEK stored in HSM under strict access workflows (manual, SLA'd, with multi-signer approval).
tasks: Design API: key management endpoints and deletion workflow (design doc link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/crypto-shred-coordinator).
Implement DEK creation + wrap/unwrap library (golang) with pluggable KMS interface.
Add field-level config to ingestion producers to mark sensitive fields and required tokenization mode (deterministic | nondeterministic).
Build Coordinator service: schedule, run, and audit delete jobs. Persist job state and attach attestation on completion.
Integrate with audit-log service: append deletion anchors and signed metadata.
Develop backfill rewrap worker with checkpointing and throttles for large partitions.
Create test harness for attempted recovery after KEK/DEK destruction to assert failure modes.
Update Console and infra docs; prepare runbook for legal requests and escrow process.
Security review and threat model update for key material lifecycle and operator access.
End-to-end performance benchmark and add metrics to Redwood Console (ingest latency, key ops/sec, deletion job time).
notes: Design tradeoffs: crypto-shredding gives a stronger deletion guarantee than logical deletion but increases complexity (KMS dependency, key-rotation, potential for accidental data loss).

We must balance deterministic tokenization (needed for joins/rollups) versus nondeterministic wrapping (better privacy). Consider hybrid: deterministic tokens for hashing-only joins (salted per-tenant) and DEK-wrapped ciphertext for raw PII fields.
Escrow policy: to support lawful recovery we need an out-of-band multi-signer HSM process. This must be gated and recorded in audit logs with human approvals.

Operational hazards: accidental KEK destruction could be catastrophic. Add pre-destroy checks, quorum, and a short grace period where KEKs are marked 'pending_destroy' before irreversible destroy, unless legal-hold excepts the scope.
Compatibility: Private deployments will require HSM provider adapters; design the KMS abstraction early to avoid coupling to a single cloud provider.
Cost: wrapping per-field increases API KMS calls. We should batch DEK generation and reuse per-tenant per-day where policy allows to reduce KMS cost.
Audit anchors: use SHA256 hashes of deletion metadata and append to our immutable audit ledger; include a signed attestation that external auditors can verify against the ledger root.
Related legal mapping: GDPR right-to-erasure covered via KEK/DEK destruction; CCPA subject deletion covered; we need legal signoff for escrow procedures and evidence format.
progress_updates: 2025-02-14: Spike completed: DEK wrap/unwrap PoC using AWS KMS; p50 latency uplift ~9ms for single-field wrap. - Aisha

review_feedback: Security: require HSM-backed KEKs for enterprise/private customers and mandate 'no-auto-destroy' flag during initial rollout for hosted customers.
Privacy: prefer default nondeterministic wrapping for free-tier customers to minimize re-identification surface.
Infra: add a throttled queue for KMS calls to avoid exceeding provider rate limits; include local LRU cache of DEKs for short-lived unwrap to reduce KMS calls.
PM: surface deletion attestation in Console UI and provide downloadable certificate for compliance teams.
qa_plan: Unit tests for wrap/unwrap library against multiple KMS adapters (AWS KMS, Vault, HSM emulator).
Integration test that simulates key destroy and verifies ciphertext cannot be recovered (attempt unwrap must error deterministically).
Chaos test: simulate race where backfill is in-flight during key rotation and ensure Coordinator handles rekeying safely.
End-to-end privacy regression tests: group-by and joins with deterministic tokens produce identical aggregates to unwrapped baseline within numeric tolerance.
